appliedDeltas.summary: ToolResultMessage now carries optional tool-execution Usage without adding it to main LLM context accounting.
Responses call_id and item_id are jointly sanitized; long combined identities use an eight-character deterministic hash and stay within 40 characters.
Generic API-key and Amazon Bedrock stored credentials propagate provider-scoped env alongside resolved auth while keeping source labels secret-free.
ModelsStoreEntry adopts the optional Last-Modified timestamp and preserves it through scoped store round-trips; no conditional-fetch behavior is claimed.
Context overflow classification recognizes DashScope and Qwen input-range errors while retaining rate-limit exclusions.

decisions.reason: The fixed upstream commit tracks provider and structural .models.ts sources but ignores and omits src/providers/data/qwen-token-plan*.json. RunLedger therefore does not invent the 15-model value catalog or register a provider whose generated values cannot be reproduced from the fixed snapshot.
RunLedger is a single-package governed runtime with its own CLI and exports; pi coding-agent convenience facades are outside the provider abstraction boundary.
The pi-ai core exports remain present, while RunLedger intentionally adds runtime, storage, daemon, verification, and governed-control-plane exports.

These generated differences come from mutable remote catalog inputs unrelated to the six bounded deltas. They remain at the reviewed RunLedger baseline until generator inputs are pinned and regenerated as a separate catalog change.

The fixed upstream and RunLedger models.ts are byte-identical and do not implement Last-Modified conditional requests. This slice adopts metadata storage only and makes no stale/cache-refresh or conditional-fetch parity claim.

messageEventTransformations.summary: Provider Message and AssistantMessageEvent contracts remain byte-identical except for the adopted ToolResult usage field and the explicitly deferred Qwen provider identifiers. Provider adapters normalize transport-specific identities but do not claim session-level safe model switching.

behaviors.summary: AssistantMessageEventStream and event shapes are byte-identical to the fixed pi-ai snapshot.
Optional tool-execution usage survives message serialization but provider context conversion emits only tool content and identity, so it is not folded into main LLM usage.
Pipe-separated Responses identities preserve call and item uniqueness through the shared transform callback, including deterministic shortening for the Chat Completions limit.
RunLedger runtime adapters consume the provider Message/Event surface separately; this manifest does not treat best-effort provider normalization as proof of session-level model-switch compatibility.

license.conclusion: The fixed pi-ai snapshot and RunLedger package both declare MIT; the bounded source adaptations are license-compatible and retain upstream provenance in this manifest.
